summary: An 80-ft tower with a steel house on top, nearing completion south of Port St. Joe in August 1967; no later source found.

events.note: Panama City Herald, August 15, 1967, reported the tower nearing completion; the source gives no completion date.

evidence.supports: Tower south of Port St. Joe on U.S. Highway 98, nearing completion in August 1967
evidence.quote: nears completion at Odena, south of Port St. Joe on U.S. Highway 98.

evidence.supports: Steel house perched atop an 80-foot tower
evidence.quote: The steel house perched atop the 80-foot tower

evidence.supports: Florida Forestry employees to use the tower to watch for smoke
evidence.quote: will be used by Florida Forestry employes in their daily vigil for tell-tale wisps of smoke indicating a forest fire.

evidence.supports: Would replace the current tower near 11-Mile
evidence.quote: This tower will replace the present tower near 11-Mile, Forestry officials said.

evidence.supports: Listing is the site's only entry; it has no present-day account of the site

sources.title: Odena #2 - Forest Lookouts
sources.publisher: Forest Lookouts website, quoting the Panama City Herald (August 15, 1967)

notes_for_editor: Single source: a volunteer lookout listing quoting a 1967 Panama City Herald article; the newspaper itself was not opened. The article calls the tower nearly complete, so the 1967 event is logged as 'other' (nearing completion), not 'built'; no completion date is known. Completion date, staffing history and fate are not in any source found. The listing is titled 'Odena #2' while the record says 'Odena'; the 1967 tower may be the second tower at the site, which is unconfirmed. The older tower near 11-Mile is not in our records and was not researched. A web search for the Odena tower also returned Ôdena, a town in Spain, which is unrelated.
